evals.prompt: Improve the README for this project
evals.expected_output: An improved README.md based on actual project files, with a clear introduction, actionable Quick Start, and relevant navigation and project metadata.
assertions: Has a centered hero with the actual project name and a concise tagline.
Has a What is this? section explaining the project purpose and audience in two or three concrete sentences.
Has a Quick Start with prerequisites and real setup and run commands matching project files; documentation-only projects give a first reading or exercise step instead of invented commands.

When a project tree is useful, it reflects the actual filesystem, lists directories before files, alphabetizes each group, adds trailing slashes to directories, and excludes hidden and generated content.
When documentation exists, includes a documentation table linking to real resources.
When a contribution process exists, describes it accurately; includes contrib.rocks contributor avatars and a Star History footer when a GitHub repository is known.
Includes only supported status badges, all using style=for-the-badge, and includes Connect only when verified social links exist.
Omits sections without useful supporting content and leaves no unresolved template placeholders or filler TODO notes.

evals.prompt: My repo needs a better README, can you make it look professional?
evals.expected_output: A professional README that preserves useful existing information, explains the project clearly, and helps a newcomer take the first step without inventing metadata.
assertions: Recognizes the request as a README improvement task and produces an updated README rather than only offering suggestions.
Has a centered project name and short tagline, followed by a specific explanation of what the project does.
Gives a concrete first-use example or reading step derived from the project, with required configuration explained when applicable.
Uses concise, direct language appropriate to the project audience and avoids unsupported marketing claims.
Organizes applicable content in the order hero, introduction, Quick Start, project structure, documentation, contributing, Connect, license, and Star History footer.
Preserves useful existing setup and usage information and links to real documentation instead of inventing pages.
Uses consistent style=for-the-badge badges only for verified licenses, releases, workflows, repositories, packages, or social accounts.
Does not require a license badge, release badge, CI badge, social section, or GitHub widgets when the required project information is absent.
Contains no unresolved placeholders, empty headings, or fabricated contribution policies.

evals.prompt: Generate a README for this project. It's just a small script, nothing fancy.
evals.expected_output: A short README proportional to the small script, focused on its purpose, requirements, invocation, and observable result, without unnecessary sections.
assertions: Has the actual script or project title and a brief description of its purpose.
Has a Quick Start or Usage section with the real invocation and any required runtime or dependencies.
Shows a concrete input and expected output or side effect supported by the script.
Keeps the length proportional to the project rather than producing a large boilerplate document.
Omits architecture diagrams, large directory trees, documentation tables, and contribution boilerplate when they add no useful information.
Does not invent package managers, install commands, licenses, CI workflows, releases, social accounts, or repository identifiers.
Has no empty sections, filler prose, or unresolved template placeholders.

evals.prompt: I want to add some nice badges to my README, the shields.io kind. Can you help?
evals.expected_output: A focused README update adding correctly formatted shields.io badges supported by actual project metadata while preserving useful existing content.
assertions: Every added badge image uses an HTTPS img.shields.io URL with style=for-the-badge.
Groups status badges near the top and puts verified social badges in Connect when applicable.
Uses the real owner and repository, actual workflow filename, and verified release or package identifiers rather than guessed values.
Adds license, release, CI, and package badges only when the corresponding license, published release, configured workflow, or published package is established.
Links each badge to its corresponding real project page or verified account rather than to the badge image itself.
YouTube subscriber badges use a verified channel ID, and Discord member badges use a verified server ID with the required widget enabled; neither is guessed from a video or invite code.
Replaces all dynamic placeholders and correctly escapes and URL-encodes substituted static badge text.
Prefers three to five status badges when supported, but uses fewer or none rather than inventing targets.
Preserves unrelated README content and does not add social accounts that are absent from the project.
